note: The attacker-controlled DNS datagram is stored as the packet buffer used by later DNS parsing and compression logic.
The compressor must ensure the computed label end stays within the packet buffer before dereferencing it; this boundary obligation is what prevents reading past the packet.
The code dereferences and compares bytes from the candidate label in the packet; if the earlier boundary check is bypassed, this becomes an out-of-bounds read.
The packet pointer is threaded into the DNS label-tracking state that is later consumed by the decoder and compressor.
The decoder is invoked with the attacker-controlled packet and the label-tracking context, reaching the compression routine on malformed input.
